title: Insets, Hinges, Ink, Peels & Typed Menus
description: A timeline inset, folding viewport segments, emoji set as ink, a clip-path corner peel, and a menu built as a dialog.

drops.title: Where the Reveal Starts
drops.description: Three columns, identical keyframes, one view() timeline each — only the inset differs, so they fire at three different moments.
drops.concept: A scroll-driven view() timeline normally spans the whole scrollport. view-timeline-inset shrinks the edges it measures against, so the entry range opens later and closes sooner without touching the keyframes or the range keywords. Three lanes show insets of 0, 22% and a live value, with a slider that takes the third negative so its cards start animating before they are on screen.

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page and watch the three columns reveal at different points.
interaction.click: Drag the inset slider to retune the third lane, including negative values.
interaction.touch: Touch-scroll works the same; the panel docks to the bottom on narrow screens.

drops.title: Layout That Folds
drops.description: Three app layouts keep their content clear of the hinge, driven by the same numbers the Viewport Segments API hands you.
drops.concept: The iPhone Duo put Device Posture and Viewport Segments in front of web developers: a page can ask whether the screen is folded and where the crease falls, then size a grid row to swallow the hinge. A player, a map and a reader all reflow around a fold you can move and thicken, and a readout reports what the browser you are actually using says about its own posture.
drops.source: Darius Cepulis — “What the iPhone Duo means for web development”

interaction.mouse: Switch between continuous and folded; drag the hinge position and thickness.
interaction.click: The posture buttons re-lay all three devices at once.
interaction.touch: Controls stack under the devices on narrow screens.

drops.title: Emoji, or Just Ink
drops.description: The same character set as a colour sticker or as monochrome type, decided in CSS instead of in your copy.
drops.concept: Dozens of characters carry both a text and an emoji presentation, and for years the only lever was a variation selector hidden in the content — U+FE0E or U+FE0F. font-variant-emoji moves that choice into the stylesheet. A specimen, a four-way comparison per glyph, and an editorial passage show why text presentation is often the typographic answer: it inherits colour and never stretches the line box.

interaction.mouse: Hover a glyph for its code point.
interaction.click: Switch the specimen between normal, text, emoji and unicode; resize it with the slider.
interaction.touch: The panel moves inline below the specimen on narrow screens.

drops.title: The Corner That Peels
drops.description: A card lifts its own corner like a sticker — one custom property drives the clip, the flap and the reveal underneath.
drops.concept: Three stacked pieces share a single length. clip-path cuts that much off the card, an absolutely positioned triangle of the same size folds back over the gap with a gradient standing in for the paper's shaded reverse, and a coloured layer shows through the hole. Because it is all one custom property, the whole gesture transitions — and in proximity mode it tracks how close the pointer is to the corner.

interaction.mouse: Hover any of the six cards; in proximity mode the fold follows the pointer.
interaction.click: Retune corner size and duration, move the peel to another corner, or switch the trigger.
interaction.touch: Without hover the cards rest part-peeled so the effect still reads.

drops.title: The Menu You Type Into
drops.description: A filterable menu built as a dialog with a search field: focus stays put, the highlight rides aria-activedescendant, and Tab walks out.
drops.concept: Filterable menus usually get built as comboboxes, and then the keyboard model fights the filtering. Base UI's answer is to treat the thing as a dialog with a search field. DOM focus never leaves the input; arrow keys move aria-activedescendant instead. Home and End jump to the first and last item only while the field is empty — once you type they belong to the caret. Every submenu gets its own search field, and focus is never trapped.
drops.source: Jenna Smith & James Nelson — “Building a filterable menu” (Base UI)

interaction.mouse: Click any of the three triggers; hovering an item moves the highlight.
interaction.click: Pick an item to close the menu and return focus to the trigger.
interaction.touch: Tap a trigger, type to filter, tap an item.
